履修条件
This course is opened to all the students that are interested in Modern Russian literature, culture and society, and are willing to reading closely literary texts.
授業概要
ドストエフスキーの短編小説および随筆を講読し、近代ロシアの文化と社会の関係から解読し、解釈する。各作品の記述や登場人物の心情、情景の描写などから、ロシアの社会、文化、歴史に対する理解を深め、各作品中の形式や手法、表現、表象、イメージを詳細に分析する。作品で表象される登場人物や社会や世界のあり方を議論し、文芸による表現、表象の実践を考察する。
Students will read Dostoevsky's short novels and essay, decipher and interpret it in terms of the relationship between culture and society in modern Russia. Students will deepen their understanding of Russian society, culture, and history through the descriptions of each work and the feelings and scenes of the characters, and analyze in detail the forms, techniques, expressions, representations, and images in each work. We will discuss the characters, society, and world represented in the works, and examine the practice of expression and representation through literature and art.

全体の教育目標
Students will obtain the historical and cultural perspectives on the 19th century Russia through literary texts. Student will be able to analyze the texts and cultural, social, and historical context as well as acquire the skills for communication and discussion with other people.
個別の教育目標
At the end of this course, students will have sufficient information about the historical, social, and cultural background of the literary texts in class. They will have also learned about various literary analytical methodologies, which will allow them to engage with the literary texts in a critical way, in order to produce meaningful discussions, presentations, and essays.
授業計画
Week 1: Introduction
Week 2: Reading of Dostoevsky's short stories (1): White Nights (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 3: Reading of Dostoevsky's short stories (2): The Crocodile (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 4: Reading of Dostoevsky's short stories (3): A Christmas Tree and a Wedding (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 5: Reading of Dostoevsky's short stories (4): Bobok (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 6: Reading of Dostoevsky's essay (1): Winter notes on Summer Impressions (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 7: Reading of Dostoevsky's essay (2): Winter notes on Summer Impressions (student's presentation and discussion)
Week 8: Conclusion and Discussion
